title: optimize CPU request path: reduce serialization, thread-pool pinning, and continuous batching
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: CPU-side work on the request path was a recurring bottleneck for small/latency-sensitive inference requests. This PR attacks three related areas: 1) redundant serialization/copying in the dispatcher and header handling; 2) suboptimal thread-pool scheduling where inference workers competed with background tasks; 3) continuous batching heuristics that caused excessive scheduling overhead for short requests. Summary of changes: removed an extra protobuf/json serialization round-trip in the request dispatcher; introduced a zero-copy request buffer abstraction for headers and routing metadata; reworked the thread pool to support per-socket worker pools and explicit thread affinity/pinning utilities; introduced a lightweight affinity-aware task queue to keep KV-cache and IO background work off inference worker cores; tuned continuous batching window heuristics (adaptive short-window for <32-token requests) and added a greedy coalescing path for tight latency SLOs; added microbenchmarks and end-to-end perf tests; added rollout/canary gating. Results: on standard CPU-only canary (c6i.4xlarge equivalent) P95 latency for 8-token requests reduced by 18%; median latency reduced by 25%; throughput for small requests increased by 24% under steady load; system CPU user+sys time for request path reduced by ~32% on our bench. Rollout plan: canary on staging (2 days), gradual ramp to 20% prod with latency SLO monitoring, fallback to previous thread-pool config if regressions observed. Checklist: perf microbench added; unit tests added; integration perf suite passed on rerun; docs updated. Related: ENG-1876 and ENG-1902.
